cluster.get_pods.answers: which pods exist for a workload right now, and their names for a follow-up logs/exec call
cluster.get_pods.never_for: replica liveness by the toolkit's own definition — that is redis.PerInstance/InstanceIndex; a pod can be Running with an unregistered app

cluster.logs.answers: a pod's stdout/stderr, including its startup window
cluster.logs.never_for: aggregated run history across replicas or time — that is Elasticsearch

cluster.rollout_status.answers: whether a deployment/statefulset rollout has finished and how many replicas are ready
cluster.rollout_status.never_for: whether a ready replica has actually registered against the app — Running/Ready is a kubelet fact, not an application one

cluster.get_json.answers: a resource's full manifest — image, env, resource limits, owner references
cluster.get_json.never_for: the resource's runtime health — a manifest is the desired/last-applied state, not a probe result

api.health.ready.answers: whether this replica is currently admitted to serve/consume — the one probe allowed to sit red on a dependency outage
api.health.ready.never_for: concluding a processor crashed from Running/NotReady with 0 restarts alone — that is expected while it waits for registration, not a fault; check the deploy log window before treating it as one

api.health.live.answers: whether the process itself is alive, independent of any dependency's health
api.health.live.never_for: readiness — a live-but-not-ready replica is normal and expected, not a fault

api.health.startup.answers: whether host initialization has completed, including migrations — the probe with a finite budget
api.health.startup.never_for: an ongoing dependency outage after startup — that moved to /health/ready, which has no budget to exhaust
